# Rifleman
The backbone of the platoon. Riflemen are the most common role on both GOVFOR and OPFOR: you follow orders, pull security, carry the fight to the enemy and hold what your platoon takes. You don't need special training for anything in this guide.
Every platoon plays the rifleman the same way. Only the names change: the vendors, the rifle, your rank and your uniform depend on which unit your side is fielding that round. The examples below use the US Colonial Marines.
## Waking Up - On most maps you start aboard your side's ship and fly down by dropship. On a few maps you start already planetside. - You wake up hungry and thirsty. Grab something to eat and drink before you deploy. - Snack, drink and cigarette vendors cost money. Your ID card's bank account starts with a little cash, and vendors take cash first, then charge the rest to your ID. - You spawn with only your ID card and headset. Everything else comes from your platoon's vendors.
## Gearing Up Your gear is free. Each vendor lets you take a limited amount, so choose carefully. Items marked as [color=green]recommended[/color] are what a rifleman should grab first.
### Apparel Vendor
Take one item from each section: fatigues and a webbing, boots, gloves, a helmet, armor, a backpack, a belt and a pouch. A magazine belt and a magazine pouch keep your reloads close at hand.
### Weapons Rack
Pick [bold]one primary weapon kit[/bold], [bold]one sidearm[/bold] and [bold]one attachment[/bold]. A kit is a case with the gun and a load of magazines. Empty kits left on the ground despawn after a minute, so you don't need to carry the case around.
The rack also has spare magazines. Load your gun before you leave.
### Equipment Vendor
The equipment vendor's motto says it all: prioritize medical supplies, a ration pack, an e-tool and sandbags.
- An [bold]IFAK[/bold] (infantry first aid kit) is the single most important thing you carry. See [textlink="Infantry First Aid" link="CMUGuideMedicalInfantry"]. - A [bold]gas mask[/bold] and spare [bold]filters[/bold], or a field oxygen tank, keep out tear gas, smoke and other gases. - [bold]Hearing protection[/bold] saves your ears from gunfire and explosions. See [textlink="Hearing Loss" link="CMUGuideHearingLoss"]. - Binoculars, flares, a bayonet and zipties are all useful extras.
Requisitions vendors are locked to requisitions staff. If your squad needs something special, ask your squad leader.
## Your Rifle - [bold]Your rifle has no IFF.[/bold] Every round you fire can hit a friendly. Never shoot through your own lines, and check what's behind your target. - Carry a mix of standard and armor-piercing (AP) magazines. AP punches through armor, both the enemy's and your friends'. - An [bold]ammo box[/bold] of the right caliber refills empty magazines, so don't throw your empties away. - Don't fire your weapon aboard the ship or anywhere you haven't been told to.
## Your Squad - You are assigned to a squad. GOVFOR fields Alpha, Bravo and Charlie; OPFOR fields Sierra, Tango and Uniform. - Each squad splits into [bold]fireteams[/bold]. You're placed in one automatically when you join. Stay with your fireteam. - Your chain of command is your [bold]Fireteam Leader[/bold], then your [bold]Squad Leader[/bold], then the platoon's officers up to the [bold]Commanding Officer[/bold]. - If a squad or fireteam loses its leader for long enough, its highest-ranking member is promoted to take over. That might be you. - Your headset can track your squad leader, fireteam leader, battle buddy and landing zone. Use it to find your way back to your squad.
## Radio
- Type [bold]:h[/bold] before a message to talk on your squad's net. - On the radio, a callsign replaces your name. - Combat radio needs a nearby [bold]anchor[/bold], such as your Fireteam Leader's backpack radio, a command post mast or a vehicle radio. Stray too far from one and your headset goes quiet, which is one more reason to stick with your fireteam. - Keep the net clear. Report what you see, briefly and accurately.
See the [textlink="Communications Guide" link="AU14Comms"] for the full picture.
## Winning the Round Both sides race to complete objectives: killing, capturing, holding zones, destroying targets and fetching items. Completed objectives build up points, and once your side has enough, the [bold]Final Objective[/bold] unlocks. Complete it to win.
Picking up [bold]intel[/bold] (documents, disks and devices found around the map) earns your side the points it spends on more intel and upgrades. Grab anything that looks like intel and hand it in. See [textlink="Objectives and Intel" link="CMUGuideIntelObjectives"].
## Digging In - Use your entrenching tool to fill sandbags, then stack them into barricades. - Anyone can vault over a barricade unless it's wired with barbed wire. - Riflemen can build basic barricades from metal. Heavier fortifications like concrete barricades need more construction training, which your squad leader and combat technicians have.
See [textlink="Fortifications" link="CMUGuideEngFortify"].
## Staying Alive - Keep your IFAK stocked. Stop the bleeding first, and use a tourniquet on a limb that won't stop. - Call for a corpsman on the radio if you or a squadmate are badly hurt. - Don't wander off alone. A rifleman on their own is an easy kill; a fireteam is not.
## Useful Controls - You can set a key to [bold]open worn storage[/bold] (belts, backpacks and pouches) by hovering over the slot, under Controls > CMU. There's also an option there so clicking worn storage with an empty hand opens it instead of taking it off.
